## Observed defect and immutable source
At main `cd9435e9ca3a83e898af8ee99ee4e17a5dc6f758`, the inline [release merge wait](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/blob/cd9435e9ca3a83e898af8ee99ee4e17a5dc6f758/.github/workflows/release.yml#L386-L498) initializes `awaiting_approval=0` before the loop (line 386), sets it to 1 after any approval-pending observation (line 488), and never clears it. The timeout conditional (line 493) therefore reports historical approval state as current.

## Hosted evidence
The [release job 126121084927](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/actions/runs/41624345351/job/126121084927) reports successful automatic approval of runs 41713352866,41713352957 and41713352928 at 20:31:54–20:31:55 UTC on 2026-11-03. At 21:01:34 it reports queued required checks, no failing checks, and refused protected merge. At 21:01:35 it instead says the release did not merge because CI is awaiting workflow approval and instructs a maintainer to approve once.

Fresh 21:50 UTC readback shows [release PR 83](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/pull/83) open/blocked at `708e98cab57974fc996e4158d942dd16a5452c87`; [run 41713352866](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/actions/runs/41713352866) and [run 41713352928](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/actions/runs/41713352928) queued, and [run 41713352957](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/actions/runs/41713352957) skipped. None of those fresh reads indicates action_required. Queued checks are not green or recovery.

## Bounded reproduction
An isolated Bash fixture preserving the workflow's initialization, pending-run assignment and deadline conditional, with no gh/git/network commands, feeds a nonempty pending-run result followed by an empty result. The actual classifier remains `approval-required` although current pending approval is false. The probe exits 0. This validates diagnostic state only, not a replay of the release workflow.

## Expected, actual and impact
The workflow's own permission comment (lines 11–14) says a maintainer approval instruction is needed when its token cannot approve, and its timeout branches (lines 492–497) distinguish approval from settling/failed checks. After successful approval and a later verified empty approval state, timeout should report current settling/check state. The retained historical flag misdirects recovery toward an action already completed.

The protected-merge/publication guard worked: the failed job did not reach publication or tagging. This is a recovery-diagnostic defect, not a publication bypass, a claim of broken Azure sync, or evidence that the complete runtime acceptance gate failed. No merge, approval, rerun, provider call or publication was performed in this review.

## Acceptance and regression criteria
- Derive timeout approval diagnosis from current successfully fetched state, not whether approval was ever observed.
- Pending approval → successful automatic approval/queued or running checks → timeout must identify current settling checks rather than demand approval again.
- Still-pending approval at timeout must retain the actual pending-run link; failed state reads must remain unknown, not be treated as a verified empty result.
- Cover those transitions and a later successful merge with isolated mocked shell/API responses.
- Preserve exact-head checks, protected merge authority, approval policy, all runtime/coverage gates and no-publish/no-tag behavior on failure. Do not increase timeouts merely to hide this diagnostic.

## Deduplication and ownership
All 83 current ADO all-status issue/PR bodies and all 50 canonical PM records at the immutable default head were checked; all 50 canonical Git blob hashes verified. No ADO issue/canonical owner for this diagnostic was found. The release record [pm-ado-glif](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/blob/cd9435e9ca3a83e898af8ee99ee4e17a5dc6f758/.agents/pm/chores/pm-ado-glif.toon) tracks release approval/publication policy, not this stale timeout state.

The same defect exists in sibling [pm-linear200](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/issues/200) and was fixed in [pm-github145](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-github/issues/145) / [PR 148](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-github/pull/148). Those records own their repositories' inline release loops; this ADO workflow executes its own Bash loop, not a reusable shared release workflow. Reuse the established regression approach where appropriate, without treating another repository's fix as ADO acceptance.
